newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Mercury Energy delays NZ$100 mln bond issue.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Mercury Energy delays NZ$100 mln bond issue.

text.p: Auckland electricity company Mercury Energy has delayed its first bond issue, of NZ$100 million worth of 10-year bonds, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Wednesday.

Treasurer Gary Rohloff told NZPA there seemed to be over-supply in the corporate bond market and a 70 to 75 basis point premium to government November 2006 bonds was too high from Mercury's perspective.
"We are unable to issue our bonds into the market at the moment at a margin that we consider appropriate for a AA- (Standard and Poor's) rated credit," Rohloff said.
"We're not in a position where we need the money. We were looking at altering our maturity profile," he said.
The issue was on hold indefinitely, but Mercury would consider going ahead when demand better matched supply.
